Subject: Re: Quick Q before our procurement kickoff — data geography and subprocessors

Hi Jamie — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer up front: for Redwood hosted API, processing occurs in customer-pinned regions (we offer us, eu, and apac region endpoints) and we use cloud providers in those regions; cross-region fallback can occur for availability but is opt-in and documented in contracts. I attached a concise subprocessor inventory and a one-page processing map for your procurement packet.

Key details:
- Hosted API: primary processing locations are (by default)
  • US: AWS us-east-1 and us-west-2 (serving hosted customers in US regions)
  • EU: GCP europe-west1 and Azure northeurope (for EU tenants where requested)
  • APAC: GCP asia-southeast1 + AWS ap-northeast-1 (selected by customer region)
- Dedicated & Private: customers can run in a dedicated cluster in a cloud region we provision, or bring Redwood Private into their VPC/on-prem — in those cases data never leaves the customer region unless they authorize it.
- Cross-border transfers: for hosted customers we route by policy (region routing, cost/latency fallback). By default we aim to keep processing in the tenant region; fallback routing to another region only happens under explicit configuration or capacity/incident scenarios and is covered in the DPA.
- Encryption & keys: all in-flight traffic is TLS; customer data at rest is encrypted with AES-256. For Private/Dedicated customers we offer CMK integration (KMS/HSM) so keys never leave the customer tenancy.
- Logging & observability: trace-level telemetry (for debugging) is redacted and stored in US-only systems by default; we can build an EU-only observability pipeline for enterprise customers.

Attachments I included: redwood_subprocessors_inventory_20270522.csv, redwood_processing_map_20270522.png, and a short processing_evidence_summary.txt that lists where artifacts like logs and backups are stored and for how long. I will follow up with SOC2 Type 2 evidence after confirming with legal.

If procurement wants a one-hour call to walk through the map and confirm clauses, I can do Monday morning.

Best,

Jamie — looping in Aditya (legal) and Marissa (privacy) to provide the formal artifacts and contract excerpts. Quick answers below while legal pulls the redacted SOC2: 

- Subprocessor country detail: included in the attached CSV — we've added a new "country" column and a "purpose" column (e.g., hosting, observability, backups).
- Deletion SLA (hosted API):
  • Customer content (model inputs + outputs): default retention 30 days; on confirmed deletion request we run a purge (logical delete + overwrite of caches) and aim to complete within 72 hours for primary stores.
  • Derived telemetry/aggregated metrics: 90 days default, can be configured for enterprise contracts.
  • Backups & long-term snapshots: retention windows vary (30–90 days) and are listed in processing_evidence_summary.txt; backups are deleted on schedule and final removal may take up to 14 days depending on underlying cloud provider snapshot behavior.
- Deletion mechanism: soft-delete flag + background compaction for primary KV and object stores; overwrite/compaction for token caches; we provide an audit log record and deletion certificate on request for enterprise customers.
- Cross-border transfers & DPA clause: fallback routing is explicitly limited by the DPA and only used for resilience; we can add a contract appendix to require strict geographic-only routing for regulated customers.

Aditya / Marissa — can you drop the redacted SOC2 and a DPA excerpt into this thread (or post a secure link)? Jamie, if you prefer, I've scheduled a 10am PT slot Monday — here is the quick mutual action plan link we use for procurements: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/SLT-2027-031 (attached to the deal record).

Thanks — we'll get the artifacts to you before Monday.

Sergio
